idiom_name: final class implementing an OrderFacade trait, with collaborators wired by the composition root (constructor or using clauses)
implementation_notes: Scala hand-writes the classic structure but shortens the wiring: declare a trait for the coarse contract, implement it in a final class that takes the fine-grained services as constructor parameters, and compose the graph once at the edge of the program - the class is the boundary, the trait is the interface. Scala 3's using clauses and given instances replace the container for the parts of the graph that are context-like: a method can request a Repository in context and the composition root provides the instance, resolved at compile time rather than at startup. Keep the constructor-parameter form for collaborators that are genuinely part of the facade's identity and the using-clause form only for ambient, single-implementation context; the classic form stays justified because nothing in the language provides lifecycle, pooling or transaction demarcation.
code_sketch:
trait OrderFacade:
  def placeOrder(req: PlaceOrderRequest): OrderId

final class OrderFacadeImpl(
    pricing: PricingService, inventory: InventoryService, repo: OrderRepository)
    extends OrderFacade:
  def placeOrder(req: PlaceOrderRequest): OrderId =
    val quote = pricing.quote(req.sku, req.qty)      // coarse-grained workflow
    inventory.reserve(req.sku, req.qty)
    repo.insert(Order(req.customerId, quote))        // unit of work owned here
pitfalls: Implicit/using resolution happens at compile time, so two given instances of the same type (two Repository implementations) fail the build with a message that points at the use site, not at the wiring; keep givens in one composition object.
Making the facade a case class leaks generated equals/copy/apply into the API; a plain final class keeps the boundary closed.
Mixing effect types (Future, IO, ZIO) between the facade and its collaborators forces one to translate; pick the effect type at the boundary or the workflow becomes untestable.
